report.summary: Chunk 3 of correctness.py: implements run_node_ids, validate_task, disposable_worktree, apply_test_overlay, reference_patch, apply_patch, and Selection dataclass. Checked claims against code in this chunk.
risks: apply_patch | low | Temporary file path is predictable (NamedTemporaryFile with no dir) | Check if tempfile is configured securely
apply_patch | low | No validation that patch_bytes is a valid git patch before writing to disk | Could be mitigated by git apply's own validation

handoff.purpose: Implements core evaluation functions: running pytest, validating tasks, managing worktrees, applying overlays and patches, and defining the Selection dataclass.

symbols.name: run_node_ids
symbols.note: Runs pytest for given node ids, with solo re-run for unattributed nodes.

symbols.name: TestRunner
symbols.note: Type alias for the injectable test runner.

symbols.name: REQUIRED_FIELDS
symbols.note: Tuple of required field names for a correctness task dict.

symbols.name: validate_task
symbols.note: Validates a task dict and returns list of problems.

symbols.name: is_correctness_task
symbols.note: Checks if a dict is a correctness task by delegating to daedalus.eval.tasks.

symbols.name: disposable_worktree
symbols.note: Context manager that creates and cleans up a disposable git worktree.

symbols.name: apply_test_overlay
symbols.note: Writes test files from a given revision into the worktree.

symbols.name: reference_patch
symbols.note: Generates a git diff patch between base and reference revisions, excluding specified paths.

symbols.name: apply_patch
symbols.note: Applies a patch to the worktree using git apply.

symbols.name: Selection
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing the measurement selection with digest.

claims.text: Batch first (one interpreter start, ~2.2s on this box, measured), then RE-RUN ALONE every node the batch left unattributed.
claims.why: Code at line ~588-610 shows batch run, then loop over unattributed nodes for solo re-run.

claims.text: That fallback is not belt-and-braces, it is required: measured on this box, a single node id pytest cannot collect aborts the WHOLE invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs -- even with --continue-on-collection-errors.
claims.why: The claim about pytest behavior is not verifiable from this code; the code implements the fallback as described.

claims.text: worktree is refused if it is the primary checkout or inside it.

An EMPTY fail_to_pass is an error, not an empty success: a task with no test that must go from red to green cannot fail, and a measurement that cannot fail is the exact defect harness._recall's vacuous 1.0 already demonstrated in this repo.
claims.why: Lines ~620-627: checks for missing/empty required fields; fail_to_pass being empty would be caught by 'if not task.get(key)' for key 'fail_to_pass'.

claims.text: Every schema problem with task, or []. Never raises.
claims.why: Function returns a list, no raises in the code.

claims.text: True for a task carrying the correctness format. Mirrored in daedalus.eval.tasks so the harness can refuse to grade one with substring recall; defined there, re-exported here for callers who already have this module imported.
claims.why: The function delegates to daedalus.eval.tasks.is_correctness_task; that module is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Delegates to daedalus.kairos.worktree.GitWorktreeManager on purpose rather than shelling out to git worktree add: that class places worktrees outside the checkout, refuses an allocation whose path is repo-adjacent, and owns a recursive delete that re-verifies every component before every syscall.
claims.why: Line ~666: manager = GitWorktreeManager(repo_root); uses manager.create_worktree and cleanup_worktree.

claims.text: Its cleanup is the ONLY delete this module performs; there is no shutil.rmtree here and there must never be one.
claims.why: No shutil.rmtree appears in this chunk; cleanup is via manager.cleanup_worktree.

claims.text: The branch ref that git worktree add -b writes into the shared .git is reaped afterwards through the manager's own reap_branches, which deletes only what it allocated in THIS process and only when git itself says another ref already contains the tip.

This is SWE-bench's "test patch", and it is what makes a before-state measurable at all: the base revision predates the fix, so it also predates the fix's tests -- running a FAIL_TO_PASS node against a bare base checkout would only ever report missing.
claims.why: Function writes test files from test_revision into worktree, enabling before-state measurement.

claims.text: Bytes are copied verbatim from git (git show <rev>:<path>), never decoded and re-encoded, so line endings and encoding are exactly what the commit holds.
Raises FileNotFoundError if a path does not exist at that revision, and OverlayEscape if it would land outside the worktree.
claims.why: Line ~688-689 raises FileNotFoundError; _safe_join raises OverlayEscape (asserted from _safe_join definition elsewhere).

claims.text: The task's own test files are EXCLUDED, because they are applied separately as the overlay -- if the reference patch carried them too, the "after" run would be testing a tree the candidate path never produces, and the two arms would not be comparable.
claims.why: Lines ~705-706: args += [f':(exclude){rel}' for rel in exclude]

claims.text: A patch that does not apply is a could_not_run, never a not_fixed: "the change was rejected by git" and "the change did not fix the bug" are different facts about different things.
claims.why: Function returns error string on non-zero returncode, not a boolean.

claims.text: Immutable (frozen dataclass, tuples not lists) and digested, so "what was measured is what was declared" is checkable by a reader instead of being a claim in a docstring.
claims.why: Class decorated with @dataclass(frozen=True), fields use tuples.

claims.text: digest covers all of it. Change any node id, the base, the overlay or the timeout and the digest changes, which is what lets correctness_gate refuse a task that was verified under one selection and presented under another.
claims.why: digest is not defined in this chunk; it is likely a property or method elsewhere.

observations.what: In run_node_ids, when len(unattributed) == len(nodes) == 1, the function returns early without solo re-run, which contradicts the docstring's claim that unattributed nodes are always re-run solo.
In run_node_ids, the early return for single unattributed node does not update output with solo re-run results, potentially losing information.
In run_node_ids, containment is only updated from solo_containment if containment == 'none', otherwise the first non-'none' containment is kept. This may mask containment issues from later solo runs.

In apply_patch, the patch_path is created with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile but the file is not deleted until the finally block. If the subprocess.run raises a timeout (not caught), the file may not be cleaned up.
In apply_patch, the error message from git apply is truncated to 800 characters, which may lose important details.
